title: Con el fin de: expresar un propósito

sections.content: Con el fin de (with the aim of, in order to) introduces the purpose behind an action -- a more formal alternative to para, common in historical prose describing policy or institutional goals. It's followed by an infinitive when the subject of both clauses is the same. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Con el fin de controlar la información que llegaba a la población, estos regímenes impusieron censores oficiales en los principales medios.
items.english: With the aim of controlling the information reaching the population, these regimes imposed official censors on the main media outlets.

items.spanish: Muchos libros fueron prohibidos y quemados, con el fin de eliminar cualquier material considerado subversivo.
items.english: Many books were banned and burned, with the aim of eliminating any material considered subversive.

items.spanish: Ciertos programas académicos quedaron bajo vigilancia militar, con el fin de impedir cualquier organización política dentro de las universidades.
items.english: Certain academic programs were placed under military surveillance, with the aim of preventing any political organization within the universities.

items.spanish: Muchos exiliados continuaron denunciando la situación de sus países, con el fin de mantener viva la atención internacional.
items.english: Many exiles kept denouncing the situation in their countries, with the aim of keeping international attention alive.

sections.content: Con el fin de + infinitive requires the same subject throughout; if the subject changes, switch to con el fin de que + subjunctive instead, just like para vs. para que.
